entries.title: Sources: CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler, which would create a cybersecurity company with a combined market cap of ~$265B; ZS jumps 15%+ after hours (Bloomberg)
TML releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights 26.4B-parameter transformer that loops middle layers three times per token for better reasoning with fewer tokens (Thinking Machines Lab)
Bitcoin falls to $57,000, its lowest level in over two years; it has lost more than half its value since reaching a peak above $126,000 in October 2025 (Bloomberg)
Sources: the US SEC is probing Nvidia's accounting practices; last year, Nvidia changed how it reports revenue, removing Singapore from geographical breakdowns (Reuters)
Sources: Nvidia board's main reason for ousting Jensen Huang was his "lying" and "lack of candor" from October 2025 until this fall over the Alice Huang affair (Wired)
Nvidia shares closed down 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day; the stock fell 44% over seven weeks, pushing the company's market cap down by $2.5T (Kif Leswing/CNBC)
Sources: Helix Digital, launched by KKR to invest in data centers, is in talks to buy EdgeCore in a deal that values the data center operator at $8B to $10B (Bloomberg)
Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79B in day-one sales, surpassing the $2.9B lifetime box-office gross of the highest-grossing film Avengers: Endgame (Jennifer Maas/Variety)
Trump says he "would love to see" Jensen Huang return as CEO, saying "if they were smart", Nvidia would "accept an apology, and let him go back to work" (Bloomberg)
METR updates its time horizon plot to add judgment-heavy tasks, finding some AI capabilities still grow exponentially but models lag at designing AI evaluations (Grace Huckins/MIT Technology Review)
Sources: YouTube reaches an agreement in principle to pay ~$3B to US school districts over claims YouTube fosters addiction; a final deal may be months away (Olivia Carville/Bloomberg)
Trump says he would block US companies from building data centers overseas or impose a "tremendous tax" on them if they do (Julianna Bragg/Axios)
Investigation: companies in Alice Huang's family network have ties to Chinese military suppliers; ~$3.6B in Chinese state money flowed through the companies (New York Times)
Tom Cotton, the GOP senator who chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, says Howard Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings about AI chips being smuggled to China (Wall Street Journal)
Scott Bessent says Trump and Xi agreed that military AI decisions should involve humans, and that the spying allegations involving Alice Huang didn't come up (Reuters)
